note: The programs COP reads and how it draws them. Each program's name, family, feed, site, fresh_hours and stale_hours live in the doctrine kit's suite registry (doctrine/kit/vocab/programs.json, kit 0.4.0, 1 Nov 2026); tools/snapshot.py merges them in, and a program missing there stops the build. Colours are Okabe-Ito hues by program family (COP design spec, 29 Oct 2026); outlines carry the 3:1 contrast against each basemap. Freshness: older than fresh_hours is late, older than stale_hours (or no data at all) is stale and draws grey; it is measured from the newest data_as_of in the feed, or from the feed's own generated_at when freshness is 'feed' (for notice programs, whose items carry issue dates). country_mark says how country-level items draw: 'fill' shades the country, 'halo' rings its label point. area_style 'dashed' draws polygons as legal or administrative areas. routine_in_preset shows a program's routine items whenever its own preset is chosen (for standing notices, which are routine by nature, and Vis's forecasts); routine_label names them in the panel (default 'standing notices'). also_in shows some of a program's items in another preset as well: an item whose kind (the second part of its id) is listed and whose title or summary matches the pattern (case ignored) is tagged cop_also at build time, and that preset draws it in its own program's colour and style whatever the routine switch says; label names them in the panel (Cordon's NGA launch, space-debris and reentry warnings under 'Spectrum and space', 14 Nov 2026, with the same pattern Orbit's navwarn lane keeps). strength rules say where an anomaly's size is found; the first rule whose 'when' matches applies, and rules rank in the order listed. Strength ranks a program's own anomalies only, never across programs. Forecasts (kind forecast, from Vis, 8 Nov 2026) are never picks, which are measured anomalies only, so Vis has no strength rules; a forecast at tier warning (Vis's Amber or Red) shows in every view, and the rest show with routine items or in Vis's own preset. Blackout (12 Nov 2026, kit 0.4.3): its outage and censorship items are country-level points, so country_mark 'fill' shades the country; its providers' status items have no geometry and list under Off the map. Its items carry no measures, so it has no strength rules; its picks follow its feed's order, which is IODA outages by drop, largest first, then OONI countries by anomaly rate. Freshness 'feed', because its items keep the time of the event or the OONI day, not the run. Colour: all seven non-black Okabe-Ito hues are taken and black at country-fill opacity reads as the stale grey, so Blackout uses Paul Tol's indigo #332288 (from his colour-blind-safe muted scheme). Headwind (13 Nov 2026, kit 0.4.6): currency and local food items are country-level points, drawn as rings at the country's label point (country_mark 'halo') because a routine reading exists for about forty countries at once; energy and FAO index items have no geometry and list under Off the map. Nearly all its items are routine readings, so routine_in_preset shows them under its own preset. Its z is signed (a fall counts as much as a rise) and strength compares raw values, so it has no strength rules; its picks follow its feed's order. Freshness 'feed', because its items carry market dates and the ECB publishes on business days only. Colour: Paul Tol's wine #882255, from the same muted scheme. Orbit (13 Nov 2026, kit 0.4.8): recent orbital launches at the launch site (approximate) and scheduled launches at the pad are points; its reentry summary and catalog-change items have no geometry and list under Off the map. Every item is a routine observation, so it has no strength rules and routine_in_preset shows its items under the 'Spectrum and space' preset it shares with Noisefloor (its registry family). Freshness 'feed', because a launch item keeps the launch time and a scheduled launch keeps Launch Library 2's last update, which can be months old. Colour: Paul Tol's olive #999933, from the same muted scheme (his other hues sit too close to Okabe-Ito hues already in use).
